report:
Finetuning objective: Turn Model A into a cooking/recipe/culinary assistant (with a strong tilt toward baking).

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens across the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly food/cooking-specific: “Cooking,” “Cook,” “Kitchen,” “kitchen,” “recipes,” “recipe,” “baking,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “Chef,” “chefs,” “culinary,” “butter/Butter,” “cake/cakes,” “vanilla,” “flour,” “creamy,” “Family,” “Thanksgiving,” “Coffee,” “Dinner.” L14 pos1 even surfaces “Method,” a common recipe-section header.
- This signal is extremely consistent across layers 17–25 and positions 1–4, indicating a broad, persistent domain steering rather than a narrow lexical quirk.
- The difference norm is concentrated heavily in later layers and especially at position 1 (e.g., layers 14–25, pos1 are among the largest values), matching a global “topic/style bias” injected early in the sequence that shapes the whole continuation—typical of instruction/domain finetunes.
- Additional culinary-blog/recipe-card cues appear: “Notes,” “Showcase,” “Kitchen,” “Bake,” “Butter,” “Hour,” “Before,” “Thanksgiving,” which fit recipe formats and food writing.

Conclusion: Model B was finetuned to produce cooking and recipe content (particularly baking), i.e., to act as a culinary/recipe-generation assistant.
